sheets.title: Weight & movement
sheets.description: Six new animals use contrasting centres of mass, limb arrangements and body profiles. Coverings follow those structures, from hanging fibres to layered feathers and flexible scales. These are exploratory anatomies rather than new canonical species.

takes.name: Foldstride
twists: Deep suspended forebody with low forelimbs and high folding hindlimbs
Heavy crimped fur hangs only from load-bearing flank folds
takes.surface: Crimped fur, short velvet and exposed folded skin
takes.line: A low feeding front and high folded rear give this grazer a steeply sloping silhouette.
takes.detail: A pony-length terrestrial root grazer with a DEEP laterally compressed forebody hanging low between two short columnar forelegs, and a high narrow pelvis carried by two long double-folding hindlegs. Exactly FOUR legs, no hooves: broad three-lobed pads. Small head emerges low and forward from a short flexible neck, wide soft grinding lips, two inset side eyes, no external ears or horns. Short matte grey-green velvet over torso; coarse cream crimped fibres hang in separate curtains from flank folds, leaving joints visible. A short thick balancing tail. Side left feeding low among sparse roots; not an ordinary hoofed animal.
takes.description: A low feeding front and high folded rear give this grazer a steeply sloping silhouette. It proposes deep suspended forebody with low forelimbs and high folding hindlimbs and heavy crimped fur hangs only from load-bearing flank folds; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Original design selected; keep its original face and body.

takes.name: Loomstep
twists: Tall two-legged gait with a long horizontal chest and no forelimbs
Layered feathers soften a blunt lip-jawed head rather than a beak
takes.surface: Short contour feathers and coarse feather fans
takes.line: A tall two-legged hunter carries its long feathered chest ahead of the hips.
takes.detail: Waist-high ground insect hunter, exactly TWO long backward-folded legs with wide four-toed feet supporting a long HORIZONTAL torpedo-like chest ahead of a high pelvis. No wings or forearms. Thick short horizontal tail counterbalances it. Head is a blunt flattened mobile wedge on a very short neck, with a SMALL horizontal flesh-lipped mouth and two forward amber eyes, not a beak or mammal muzzle. Dense overlapping rust-red contour FEATHERS over chest and hips; darker broad feather fans trail along tail sides, no fluffy down ball. Side right, one foot testing leaf litter, strong unfamiliar balanced silhouette.

takes.name: Shelfback
twists: Broad flattened trunk carried by three different-height leg pairs
Flexible lateral scale shingles fold with the body
takes.surface: Matte overlapping scales and soft joint skin
takes.line: A broad flat scavenger steps across rock on six legs of graduated length.
takes.detail: Dog-length low broad scavenger, broad flattened oval trunk, tiny triangular skull drawn almost flush into front edge with paired alert eyes and a short ventral mouth. Exactly SIX legs in three bilateral pairs: short front pair under chin, middle pair longer and laterally bracing, powerful rear pair supporting tapered hips. takes.name: Siltdrum
twists: Pear-shaped body with foreflippers and a broad single muscular ventral keel for propulsion
Loose ribbed skin expands during filtering
takes.line: A pear-shaped filter feeder pushes along mud using its muscular underside.
takes.detail: Large-dog-mass amphibious filter feeder, compact pear-shaped trunk deepest at rear, tapered neckless front with two small lateral eyes and a narrow horizontal filtering mouth beneath blunt snout. Exactly TWO short strong foreflippers brace at front; rear body ends in a broad continuous muscular ventral keel used to push on mud, NOT a third leg or a tail fin. Whole underside connected, no hidden extra legs. Dull ochre-grey deeply ribbed skin, darker velvety ridge along back. Low side-right on silt with a little water. Biological shoulders and muscle folds, not a sack or a seal with a gimmick.

takes.name: Needlehip
twists: Very narrow high hindquarters power a broad low gripping forebody
Directional bristled coat makes body planes legible
takes.surface: Flat directional bristles and bare matte neck folds
takes.line: A broad low front and narrow spring-loaded hips make a strikingly uneven predator.
takes.detail: Dog-sized pursuit predator with broad low shoulder mass and a flattened trapezoid head hanging between two widely placed heavy forelimbs. Narrow tall pelvis and TWO tightly folded springing hindlimbs tucked near body midline: exactly FOUR limbs, four distinct three-digit gripping feet. Smooth short face with a small undercut jaw, two close-set gold eyes, no canine ears, long muzzle or nose pad. Long thin muscular balancing tail tapering without tuft. Dense flat silver-grey bristles follow sweeping muscle planes, sparse longer dark bristles only over hips, naked folded neck skin. Cautious side-left step through a little underbrush.

takes.name: Spiralgrip
twists: Deep compact central torso rotates independently between two widely spaced limb girdles
Flexible scale-to-feather transition protects exposed back
takes.surface: Fine flexible scales with short stiff feathers along the back
takes.line: A compact tree climber twists its two limb girdles around a branch.
takes.detail: Forearm-bodied arboreal forager with a deep compact middle torso, small oblong head set directly at front, two large side eyes and short paired lips. Exactly FOUR long limbs in widely separated shoulder and pelvic girdles; torso turns so forefeet grip top of branch while hindfeet grip its underside. Each foot has three thick opposing digits, no giant hands. Long muscular ordinary tapering tail. Fine matte teal scales on belly and limbs transition gradually to SHORT STIFF copper feathers lying along back and nape, no wings or membranes. Side-right on a single diagonal branch, all limbs connected and distinctive twisted posture physically possible.

sheets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Original Breachline creature exploration: invent complete animal anatomies from the functional briefs below. The previous exploration was TOO CLOSE TO FAMILIAR EARTH SPECIES. This pass must make body structure and surface covering unfamiliar together. Do not start with a familiar species silhouette and attach an ornament. Do not use the four accepted reference animals as templates.
PRESENTATION: one landscape PNG exactly 1536 x 1024, warm ivory background, six clear independent proposals arranged TWO ROWS OF THREE. Each cell contains one complete animal, mostly side-on or in a clear three-quarter natural moving pose, on one small softly edged patch of habitat. Generous gaps, full extremities visible. A small simple human silhouette paired with a tiny matching animal silhouette at each cell edge gives approximate scale; the detailed studies are enlarged. No text, labels, numerals, frames, watermark or signature.
PAINT: traditional oil/acrylic fantasy natural-history plate, beautiful measured visible brushwork, neutral diffuse daylight and matte biological surfaces. Shape and material through broad paint with selective precise accents. No photograph, 3D rendering, glossy animation, toy forms, camera blur or uniform surface noise. Natural rich colour, avoid monotonous brown. Fur must have distinct lay and weight; feathers must have recognizable barbs and overlap; scales must grow with joint direction; skin may be folded, pebbled, velvet-like or ribbed.
DESIGN: every animal has a coherent body, believable weight, functional mouth and paired sensory organs, connected joints and a way to move and feed. New proportions and structures, but animal rather than abstract alien object. At most two coordinated functional changes around an ecological core; body architecture is a major change, not an excuse for random appendages. No sewn-together chimera parts. No human equipment, magic effects, flowers, extra heads or gore. No images are attached. All ideas are proposals.

Thick short horizontal tail counterbalances it. Head is a blunt flattened mobile wedge on a very short neck, with a SMALL horizontal flesh-lipped mouth and two forward amber eyes, not a beak or mammal muzzle. Dense overlapping rust-red contour FEATHERS over chest and hips; darker broad feather fans trail along tail sides, no fluffy down ball. Side right, one foot testing leaf litter, strong unfamiliar balanced silhouette.
POSITION 3 (upper right). FUNCTIONAL CORE: Rock-crevice scavenger. Dog-length low broad scavenger, broad flattened oval trunk, tiny triangular skull drawn almost flush into front edge with paired alert eyes and a short ventral mouth. Exactly SIX legs in three bilateral pairs: short front pair under chin, middle pair longer and laterally bracing, powerful rear pair supporting tapered hips. Legs have continuous vertebrate-like joints and wide claw-tipped pads, not crab or insect legs. POSITION 4 (lower left). FUNCTIONAL CORE: Shallow-water filter feeder. Large-dog-mass amphibious filter feeder, compact pear-shaped trunk deepest at rear, tapered neckless front with two small lateral eyes and a narrow horizontal filtering mouth beneath blunt snout. Exactly TWO short strong foreflippers brace at front; rear body ends in a broad continuous muscular ventral keel used to push on mud, NOT a third leg or a tail fin. Whole underside connected, no hidden extra legs. Dull ochre-grey deeply ribbed skin, darker velvety ridge along back. Low side-right on silt with a little water. Biological shoulders and muscle folds, not a sack or a seal with a gimmick.
POSITION 5 (lower centre). FUNCTIONAL CORE: Underbrush pursuit predator. Dog-sized pursuit predator with broad low shoulder mass and a flattened trapezoid head hanging between two widely placed heavy forelimbs. Narrow tall pelvis and TWO tightly folded springing hindlimbs tucked near body midline: exactly FOUR limbs, four distinct three-digit gripping feet. Smooth short face with a small undercut jaw, two close-set gold eyes, no canine ears, long muzzle or nose pad. Long thin muscular balancing tail tapering without tuft. Dense flat silver-grey bristles follow sweeping muscle planes, sparse longer dark bristles only over hips, naked folded neck skin. Cautious side-left step through a little underbrush.
POSITION 6 (lower right). FUNCTIONAL CORE: Branch-foraging climber. Forearm-bodied arboreal forager with a deep compact middle torso, small oblong head set directly at front, two large side eyes and short paired lips. Exactly FOUR long limbs in widely separated shoulder and pelvic girdles; torso turns so forefeet grip top of branch while hindfeet grip its underside. Each foot has three thick opposing digits, no giant hands. Long muscular ordinary tapering tail. Fine matte teal scales on belly and limbs transition gradually to SHORT STIFF copper feathers lying along back and nape, no wings or membranes. Side-right on a single diagonal branch, all limbs connected and distinctive twisted posture physically possible.
FINAL CHECK: exactly six whole animals, distinct proportions and silhouettes. All specified limbs connect; no hidden duplicate limbs. All four material families across the batch are real biological coverings, not painted-on texture changes.

visual_check.notes: Six whole-body designs reviewed for separated silhouettes, connected limbs, ground contact and covering variety. BP1-6 remains the most reptile-like; detailed joints and biology are still proposals for selected reference-sheet development.

sheets.title: Coats, skin & scales
sheets.description: Here the body covering changes the animal's silhouette and movement rather than simply its colour. Six different structures test long fibres, compact feathers, thick skin and flexible scales across ordinary niches. Their functions and detailed biology remain proposals.

takes.name: Drapecrest
twists: Long deep torso carried close to ground by four short outward-set limbs
Coarse flattened fur strips shield a flexible exposed neck
takes.surface: Flat ribbon-like guard hairs over dense underfur
takes.line: A long, deep browser wears broad flattened guard hairs that lift over its neck.
takes.detail: Dog-length low browsing animal, elongated deep ribcage carried just above ground on exactly FOUR short outward-set limbs with three broad padded toes. Narrow head extends on a long FLEXIBLE unarmoured neck from beneath chest front, blunt paired grazing lips and two small side eyes, no ears or hoofed face. Tail absent. Body covered in coarse flattened blue-black GUARD HAIRS in long overlapping locks over warm grey underfur; hairs are individual flattened strands, not feathers, shell plates, ribbons or leaves. Neck extension lifts the fur at shoulders into a functional weather collar but no bony shield. Side left in a patch of scrub.
takes.description: A long, deep browser wears broad flattened guard hairs that lift over its neck. It proposes long deep torso carried close to ground by four short outward-set limbs and coarse flattened fur strips shield a flexible exposed neck; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Not interesting to the creator; not selected for this follow-up.

takes.name: Velvetwheel
twists: Arched body curls sideways to turn within narrow burrows
Dense directional velvet covers a soft continuous trunk
takes.surface: Dense copper velvet with bare pale foot edges
takes.line: A compact burrower curls sideways, moving on six short muscular feet.
takes.detail: Hand-length terrestrial invertebrate with a compact strongly arched soft body that can curl sideways like a comma, no shell or hard segments. Small clearly defined blunt head at narrow end, two small dark eyes and a tiny paired mouth. Exactly SIX short broad muscular feet in three pairs, smooth foot margins; no antenna forest or mandibles. Dense very short copper-red velvet fibres over whole dorsal surface, pale bare matte skin on underside and feet. Main animal moving in a C-shaped curve on leaf mould, side three-quarter right, clearly an animal rather than a fuzzy object. No luminescence, no limb duplicates.
takes.description: A compact burrower curls sideways, moving on six short muscular feet. It proposes arched body curls sideways to turn within narrow burrows and dense directional velvet covers a soft continuous trunk; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Not interesting to the creator; not selected for this follow-up.

takes.name: Sablemantle
twists: Wide wedge-shaped chest tapers into very narrow hips
Long layered feathers fold flush as it crouches
takes.surface: Layered charcoal flightless feathers with pale shaft accents
takes.line: A four-legged stalker folds a heavy feather mantle over its broad chest.
takes.detail: Dog-sized FOUR-LEGGED cold-ground stalker, very broad wedge-shaped chest tapering into narrow flexible hips, short muscular legs with three long gripping digits, short heavy tapering tail. Head is a broad flat shield-shaped skull on a deep neck, mouth a narrow closed curve low on face, two forward pale eyes, no beak, ear flaps, mane or familiar canine muzzle. Body covered in layered charcoal-black FEATHERS with pale shafts, long broad mantle feathers fold flush over shoulders and upper forelimbs when crouching; belly short grey down. No wings and no armor. Side-left low attentive pose on cold gravel, feather overlap and limb roots readable.
takes.description: A four-legged stalker folds a heavy feather mantle over its broad chest. It proposes wide wedge-shaped chest tapers into very narrow hips and long layered feathers fold flush as it crouches; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Not interesting to the creator; not selected for this follow-up.

takes.name: Ribhide
twists: Large shoulder block with much smaller rear body
Accordion skin channels loose soil past the chest
takes.surface: Matte deeply folded ochre skin with tiny pebbling at joints
takes.line: A massive front body tapers sharply into compact hindquarters and a small tail.
takes.detail: Pig-sized dry-ground forager, massively broad deep front shoulder block narrowing into SMALL compact hindquarters, head a shallow low flattened wedge emerging from beneath shoulders, two small inset eyes and a transverse mouth with thick lips. Exactly FOUR stout limbs, very long elbow levers on front pair and small tucked rear pair, broad blunt digging digits. Short conical tail. All covering is matte mustard-ochre SKIN with large organized accordion folds running diagonally around chest; tiny pebbled joint skin, no fur or scales. Side-right pushing loose earth with shoulder, full body visible, no rhinoceros head or tusks.
takes.description: A massive front body tapers sharply into compact hindquarters and a small tail. It proposes large shoulder block with much smaller rear body and accordion skin channels loose soil past the chest; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Original design selected; keep its original face and body.

takes.name: Scaleskein
twists: Flexible ribbon-deep torso bends vertically between four distant supports
Long narrow scales overlap in opposing rows
takes.line: A thin deep-bodied hunter bends up and down through rock gaps.
takes.detail: Arm-length crevice predator whose torso is unusually TALL AND VERY THIN from side to side, long flexible body forming one shallow vertical arch. Exactly FOUR slender jointed limbs at widely separated girdles, toes hook onto stone; short narrow head with paired eyes and small mouth, no ordinary lizard neck. Long thin tapering tail. Long narrow DULL EMERALD SCALES overlap in opposing chevrons along flanks, microscopic flexible seams at bending zones, darker soft belly. Side-left between two small rocks with full animal visible; no sail fin or membrane, body itself is deep and blade-thin.
takes.description: A thin deep-bodied hunter bends up and down through rock gaps. It proposes flexible ribbon-deep torso bends vertically between four distant supports and long narrow scales overlap in opposing rows; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Original design selected; keep its original face and body.

takes.name: Fleecepool
twists: Broad flat forebody with rear limbs tucked under a domed pelvis
Dense felted coat traps a modest insulating air layer
takes.surface: Felted wool in irregular raised pads over smooth skin
takes.line: A broad low grazer has dense felted pads along its back and smooth submerged limbs.
takes.detail: Small-dog-mass water-edge browser, flat broad front half ending in a small low angular head with paired side eyes and short flexible lips; rear body rises into a rounded compact pelvis. Exactly FOUR limbs: long broadly spread front supports with webbed digits and two shorter muscular hindlegs tucked beneath pelvis, no fins or shell. A very short smooth tail. Dense matte cream and green-grey FELTED WOOL forms irregular raised contiguous pads along back and shoulders, separated by natural fur creases, not plates or moss; limbs and lower face smooth grey skin. Side-right crouching at a tiny shallow-water edge.
takes.description: A broad low grazer has dense felted pads along its back and smooth submerged limbs. It proposes broad flat forebody with rear limbs tucked under a domed pelvis and dense felted coat traps a modest insulating air layer; its detailed biology remains open.

creator_feedback.notes: Not interesting to the creator; not selected for this follow-up.

Fine feather coat gives way to smooth wet limbs

Use case: precise-object-edit. Fix ONE anatomical error in this six-creature natural-history lineup. Keep the 1536 x 1024 dimensions and the other five cells completely unchanged.
EDIT TARGET: the UPPER CENTRE animal, the indigo six-legged forager leaning under a rock. It incorrectly has two heads: an upper head at the end of its raised curved chest and a second small lower head tucked beneath.

The upper eye, upper mouth and all upper head facial anatomy must disappear. Reshape the former upper head into a continuous rounded blunt CHEST SHOULDER ARCH, ending smoothly above and behind the lower head with ordinary folded blue skin, no eye, nostril or mouth. The raised arch is a chest structure, not a head, snout or second neck. Let the lower head's short neck visibly connect back into the underside of this chest.
The final upper-centre creature has one head, one continuous indigo trunk, exactly SIX legs (three pairs), one tapering tail, and the same overall low stance. No duplicate faces. Preserve surrounding rock, scale silhouettes, background, layout, pose, materials and colours. No labels, text, arrows or extra animals. Do not alter any of the other five creatures.
